testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: After changing a tire, the driver should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: The radiator cap:

options.text: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
Can be removed when the coolant is hot.
Should feel cool to touch during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be removed when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap when the cooling system is hot. Hot water and steam can escape and cause severe burns. Wait until the cap feels cool before opening it.

questions.question: What is the number one cause of death and injury in a work zone?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly near workers.

questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
Makes sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Makes drivers responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: Drivers may need to submit a written vehicle inspection report at the end of each driving day. The motor carrier must fix any safety problems listed in the report or confirm that no repairs were needed.

questions.question: You can avoid distracted driving by:
questions.explanation: To avoid distracted driving, pre-program your radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you start, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: When pulled over to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use your taillights to alert other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to alert other drivers.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers, especially when visibility is poor. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear: engine speed (RPM) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual to learn the correct RPM range and which speeds work for each gear. Time is not a factor in deciding when to shift.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: The emergency brake system is made up of:

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three braking systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on a road surface is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice that lets you see the road through it. A road with black ice may look like it is just wet. Be very careful when temperatures are below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: In cold weather, check and refill your alcohol evaporator every day. The evaporator helps prevent ice from building up in air brake systems.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, what should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving to ensure fuel reaches the engine
Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems
Start driving right after the vehicle starts

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems
questions.explanation: Before driving, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi pressure in both systems. Watch the air pressure gauges to check the pressure levels.

questions.question: Which person should NOT concern motorists as a distraction?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be cautious around people not paying attention to traffic. Drivers and pedestrians talking to others may be distracted and not notice the road. Construction workers may focus on their work instead of traffic and can distract drivers.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on long trips?
questions.explanation: Take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving at night or when you would normally be asleep increases fatigue danger.

questions.question: When you plan to change lanes, you should check your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of normal driving. When changing lanes, check them even more carefully.

questions.question: Before going downhill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Shift into a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster on the hill.

questions.question: If you need to stop on the road to unload cargo, you should:

options.text: Stop suddenly, since you are already on the road
Warn other drivers by tapping your brakes
Wave your arm out the window to get attention

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers by tapping your brakes
questions.explanation: Tap your brakes and flash your lights to warn other drivers when you slow down or stop where they may not expect it. Use this method when stopping on the road to unload cargo or passengers.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road, you must:
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: What do alcohol evaporators do?

options.text: They add alcohol to air brake systems
They are only allowed in northern parts of the state

questions.correctAnswerText: They add alcohol to air brake systems
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. They add alcohol to the brake system to help prevent ice formation.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch in the grooves

questions.explanation: During pre-trip inspection, check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in every groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Do not mix tire sizes.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be viewed as:
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers takes a driver's attention away from the road. Be extra careful around drivers who are distracted.

questions.question: If other vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane on a multilane road if your truck is slow. Let other vehicles pass you in the left lane.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than 3 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from air tanks in brake systems. Always drain the tank completely when using the drain.

questions.question: If the driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would safely cross railroad tracks at a simulated location.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, even for smaller cargo.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to between ____, a visual low pressure warning signal should already be on.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal must activate before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating when going uphill.

questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking if possible until your vehicle slows down on its own.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: Check your brakes for cracked drums, pads with oil or grease on them, and pads that are missing or worn too thin. Clean, dry pads are a sign of good brakes.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do?

options.text: It is required on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Speed up smoothly and gradually. Do not jerk the vehicle. Rough acceleration can damage engine parts.

questions.question: What endorsement do you need to carry hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: You must pass a hazardous materials endorsement test to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Create more space in front of your vehicle to help the tailgater pass safely. Driving faster will not help because they may just tailgate you at the higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What is a dual air brake system?

options.text: Two separate air brake systems that use the same controls.
One air brake system with two different sets of controls.
One system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two separate air brake systems that use the same controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems that share one set of controls. Each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually controls the front brakes and the other controls the rear brakes.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: You cannot see what is behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see what is behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because the driver cannot see everything behind them. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: What does hanging meat in a refrigerated truck require?

options.text: It is good practice for inexperienced drivers.
It is illegal in most states.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and swings during driving, which makes it hard to control the vehicle. You must drive carefully with this cargo.

questions.question: To know if a vehicle can handle a load, you need to know:

options.text: The tire rating for the front tires only.
The tire rating for the rear tires only.

questions.explanation: You must know the weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry. Check the suspension system rating to make sure your vehicle is not overloaded.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be at the end of a basic controls test?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: You must finish each exercise with your vehicle in the exact position the examiner told you. If you do not complete the exercise exactly as described, you may fail the basic controls test.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: An air brake system includes an air compressor, governor, storage tanks, tank drains, alcohol evaporator, safety valve, brake pedal, foundation brakes, supply gauges, application gauge, low air pressure warning, stop light switch, front brake limiting valve, spring brakes, and parking brake controls.

questions.question: You must always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must stop within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information at the crossing and call 911.

questions.question: When traveling below 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance per 10 feet of vehicle length. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: When going down a steep grade, shift to a lower gear:
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before starting a downhill grade. Gravity will increase your speed going downhill.

questions.question: Interstate carriers must display what information on both sides of a CMV?
questions.explanation: Federal regulations require the USDOT number to be displayed on both sides of every vehicle in a carrier's fleet.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
Complete it as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Use the same inspection process every time. This habit helps you remember all the important checks.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving away is safer than stopping. You can turn away from an object faster than you can come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Wheel rims that have been welded should:

options.text: Be placed on rear tires only.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are unsafe and should not be used.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe operation. Perform routine inspections before driving a commercial vehicle.
